metadata.title: Quality Evaluation of LLM-based Generated Test Case: A Literature Review
metadata.journal: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data and Software Engineering (ICoDSE)

abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied in automated test case generation. Unlike traditional testing, quality evaluation of their outputs requires novel approaches due to the non-deterministic nature of LLMs and the risks of bias and hallucination. This study conducts a systematic literature review of 25 publications (2020–2025) to examine quality criteria, evaluation metrics, and heuristics in LLM -based test case generation. Findings show that correctness/accuracy and coverage metrics remain dominant, yet there is a growing focus on bias and hallucination detection. Effective heuristics include human-in-the-loop evaluation, gold standard comparison, and multi-agent frameworks. The review highlights emerging frameworks integrating ethical and safety criteria, underscoring the need for comprehensive evaluation to ensure reliability and fairness in automated test generation.

key_findings.claim: Correctness/accuracy and coverage metrics remain the dominant quality criteria used to evaluate LLM-generated test cases.
key_findings.context: Finding from systematic review of 25 publications (2020–2025) on LLM-based test case generation.

key_findings.claim: There is a growing focus on bias and hallucination detection as quality concerns in LLM-generated test cases.
key_findings.context: Trend identified across 25 reviewed publications spanning 2020–2025.

key_findings.claim: Human-in-the-loop evaluation, gold standard comparison, and multi-agent frameworks are effective heuristics for evaluating LLM-generated test case quality.
key_findings.context: Synthesized from systematic review; no individual study results reported in abstract.

key_findings.claim: Emerging evaluation frameworks are integrating ethical and safety criteria into the assessment of LLM-generated test cases.
key_findings.context: Identified as an emerging trend in the reviewed literature; underscores need for reliability and fairness considerations.

key_findings.claim: Quality evaluation of LLM-based test case generation requires novel approaches beyond traditional testing metrics due to LLM non-determinism, bias risk, and hallucination.
key_findings.context: Motivation stated in abstract for conducting the systematic review.

llm_extraction.methods_summary: Systematic literature review of 25 peer-reviewed publications published between 2020 and 2025. The review examined quality criteria, evaluation metrics, and heuristics used in LLM-based test case generation. No additional methodological detail (search databases, inclusion/exclusion criteria, PRISMA compliance) is available from the abstract alone.
llm_extraction.limitations: Only the abstract is available, so detailed methodological limitations cannot be assessed. From what is reported: (1) the review covers only 25 publications, which may not be exhaustive; (2) no PRISMA flowchart or inter-rater reliability information is mentioned; (3) the 2020–2025 window may underrepresent very recent advances; (4) the abstract does not specify which LLMs or test generation domains were covered, limiting generalizability assessment.

methodology_details.approach: Systematic literature review synthesizing quality criteria, evaluation metrics, and heuristics from 25 publications on LLM-based test case generation (2020–2025).
methodology_details.reproducibility_notes: Search strategy, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and screening protocol not described in the abstract.

domain_specific_fields.dataset: 25 publications on LLM-based test case generation (2020–2025)
